problem: Prior VLN agents on R2R fuse vision and language weakly and produce long trajectories, and they generalize poorly from seen to unseen environments.
motivation: An agent must jointly understand visual and language information to navigate an unknown indoor environment. Practical navigation also needs short trajectories, and a gap between seen and unseen performance limits deployment.
key_idea: Use attention-based cross-modal fusion so visual features carry language information and vice versa, train with A2C reinforcement learning to shorten trajectories, and add Cro-Speaker data augmentation to narrow the seen/unseen gap.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation details can be cited. The abstract claims that bidirectional cross-modal attention raises SR, that A2C-based action constraints shorten trajectory length, and that Speaker and Cro-Speaker augmentation improve generalization across known and unknown environments.
method: Cross-modal feature fusion: attention modules make visual features contain language information and language features contain visual information, capturing their alignment.
A2C reinforcement learning: an advantage actor-critic objective constrains action selection to shorten trajectory length.
Cro-Speaker data augmentation: a proposed method for generating additional instruction-trajectory data to reduce the seen/unseen gap.
Training strategies: SD (Speaker augmentation), CSD (Cro-Speaker augmentation) and SCSD (both combined).

setting.backbone: Attention-based cross-modal fusion network trained with A2C (details not given in the abstract)
setting.training_data: R2R training data plus Speaker and Cro-Speaker synthetic augmented instructions (scale not stated in the abstract)
setting.observation: panoramic RGB views at the current viewpoint plus language instruction (assumed from the R2R setting)
